newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis to break-even in 18 mths.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis to break-even in 18 mths.

text.p: Australis Media Ltd managing director Neil Gamble said Friday's approval by bond holders for an equity injection could allow the pay television group to show profits sometime in calendar 1998.

"We should break-even in about 18 months," Gamble told Reuters. "Those funds should carry us through to break even point, so there won't be any need to raise new capital unless we change our business plan," Gamble said.
Earlier bond holders approved the company's US$250 million recapitalisation plan, while its satellite joint venture with Optus Vision received regulatory approval.

Gamble said the court decision earlier today favouring Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd's plans to form a rebel rugby league competition, known as Super League, was also a plus for Australis as it planned to broadcast Super League games.

Last month, Australis reported a net loss of A$251.69 million in the year to June 30, 1996, compared with a net loss of A$122.05 million in the 1994/95 year. Australis has said that it expects to make losses until the 1997/98 year to June 30.
Gamble said approval of the recapitalisation plan also boosted the group's marketing of its proposed US$150 million note issue.
"The note issue would be the final touch on our capital raising plans," Gamble said

Gamble said the satellite joint venture with Optus Vision would also improved Australis' cash flow and reduce costs by about A$25 million a year due to the sharing of satellite infrastructure and management.

Following the recapitalisation, Lenfest Communications Inc, 50 percent owned by Tele-Communications Inc, will have a 32.8 percent economic interest in Australis and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd will have a 10 percent economic interest in Australis. --Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
